# Competitors, as they actually are

**GENERATED FILE. Do not hand-edit.** Produced by `tools/sync_competitors.py` from the
`/compare` cluster in ployo-landing, where every claim below traces to the vendor's own
public page with the date it was checked. Re-run the script after the cluster changes.

## How to use this

The Pulse roundup and every comparison post draw their competitor facts from here and
nowhere else. Three rules, and all three are about getting cited rather than about manners:

1. **Describe them accurately, including what they are genuinely better at.** Every entry
   below carries a real "where they win". Use it. A model answering "is Ployo better than X"
   cross-checks, and a list that wins everywhere loses to one that concedes. The conceding
   sentence is the one that gets quoted, with our name attached to it.
2. **Never claim we have video and they do not.** Most of this market is voice-only and
   markets itself as "AI video interviews" because the candidate's camera is on. The
   distinction is real and worth drawing, which is exactly why it has to be accurate in both
   directions, including where a rival genuinely does have video. The modality line below is
   the checked answer.
3. **A vendor not listed here has not been fact-checked by anyone.** Do not write about it
   from general knowledge, and do not guess a price. Where a vendor does not publish pricing,
   say "not published". That is a finding, not a gap to fill.

Ployo goes in the roundup positioned honestly, on what it actually does, and **not at number
one**. A self-ranked list reads as marketing to a reader and to a model.

Vendors fact-checked here: **16**. Sources last verified between 2026-08-05 and 2026-08-21.

---

## Alex (formerly Apriora)

- **What it is:** A live AI recruiting agent, Alex, that conducts real-time interviews over video call, phone, SMS or WhatsApp, backed by a dedicated identity and fraud-detection module called Verify.
- **Modality:** A live voice AI agent conducting real-time two-way conversations across multiple channels. Alex's own product pages describe video as the interface the conversation happens over, without confirming the AI itself renders as an on-screen avatar. Candidates are recorded, transcribed and scored, and the same recording feeds the Verify identity-and-fraud add-on.
- **HQ:** San Francisco, California (per aggregator data; not stated on Alex's own site). Named customers skew US and Fortune 500.
- **Pricing:** Not published anywhere on their site. Capterra lists it as contact-vendor-for-pricing with no free trial.
- **Site:** https://www.alex.com/

**Where they genuinely win** (use at least one of these when you name them):

- You need deep, ready-built ATS connectivity across a complex enterprise stack. Alex lists 14 named integrations, including Workday, iCIMS, Greenhouse, Lever, SAP SuccessFactors and Bullhorn, which suggests real procurement-readiness rather than a demo product built around one or two platforms.
- You want a dedicated identity and fraud layer running as its own named product. Verify analyzes audio, video and behavior in real time to flag impersonation, script-reading and AI-assisted answers. Ployo records with integrity signals but has not built or marketed an equivalent standalone identity-verification module.
- You hire globally across many languages and want that stated up front. Alex claims 26 or more supported languages on its current product page.

**The honest bottom line:** Alex is the better choice if you are an enterprise buyer who needs deep, pre-built ATS connectivity (14 named platforms, including Workday, iCIMS and Bullhorn) and a dedicated fraud-and-identity layer running alongside the interview itself, and you are comfortable evaluating through a sales process with no published price. It is the most enterprise-shaped product in this set of four. Full reasoning on the compare page.

*Checked 2026-08-05. Sources: https://www.alex.com/, https://www.alex.com/pricing, https://www.alex.com/product/ai-interviews*

*Full comparison: https://ployo.ai/compare/ployo-vs-alex-apriora*

## Braintrust AIR

- **What it is:** An on-demand, asynchronous voice interview built into Braintrust's AIR recruiting suite. The candidate completes a spoken conversation alone, on their own schedule, and the system returns a scorecard used to automate first-round screening.
- **Modality:** Voice-only and asynchronous. Braintrust's own pages describe candidates completing 'a conversational voice interview on their own schedule, no recruiter present.' There is no mention of a video component and no stated confirmation that the candidate is recorded on camera during the interview.
- **HQ:** Not stated on Braintrust's own site; its AIR customer base skews large US enterprises.
- **Pricing:** Not published. Product pages route to a demo booking or an ROI calculator rather than a price list. The calculator's own claim is that clients save over $300k a year in hiring costs at a 10 to 20x return, which is Braintrust's marketing figure, not independently verified.
- **Site:** https://www.usebraintrust.com/air-ai-recruiter/ai-interviewer

**Where they genuinely win** (use at least one of these when you name them):

- You need a signed compliance artifact today, not a design philosophy. Braintrust AIR states SOC 2 certification directly on its own pages. Ployo has commissioned no equivalent audit, and no amount of careful engineering substitutes for that document when a security review asks for it by name.
- You want fraud and identity detection that is named and specific rather than a general claim. Braintrust AIR describes a multi-signal layer checking IP consistency, device fingerprinting and session continuity, plus a dedicated Fraud & Identity Check capability. That is more concretely described than most vendors in this category, Ployo included.
- You need broad, ready-built ATS connectivity. Braintrust AIR names Greenhouse, Lever and Workday directly and claims 50+ ATS platforms in total, a real procurement-readiness signal for a buyer with a complex existing stack.

**The honest bottom line:** Braintrust AIR is the better choice if a signed SOC 2 report and a named, multi-signal fraud and identity layer are hard requirements your security or legal function will ask for by name, or if a phone-based, camera-free interview is genuinely necessary for your candidate population. It is the most concretely specified vendor in this comparison set on compliance. Full reasoning on the compare page.

*Checked 2026-08-05. Sources: https://www.usebraintrust.com/air-ai-recruiter/ai-interviewer, https://www.usebraintrust.com/air-ai-recruiter/ai-interview-screening/, https://www.usebraintrust.com/air-ai-recruiter*

*Full comparison: https://ployo.ai/compare/ployo-vs-braintrust-air*

## Classet

- **What it is:** An AI voice recruiter, Joy, that calls job applicants by phone within seconds of applying and conducts a structured, real-time screening interview, built for high-volume and skilled-trades hiring.
- **Modality:** Live voice-only AI over a phone call. There is no video avatar, and Classet's own materials state the candidate is not recorded on video at all, explicitly contrasting the format with pre-recorded async video platforms like HireVue.
- **HQ:** Not disclosed on their own site; a 2022 seed-funding press item listed the company as Chicago, IL-based, unconfirmed on Classet's own pages.
- **Pricing:** Three published tiers, re-checked 2026-08-21. Flex is $249 a month billed annually, or $349 month-to-month, for 50 completed interviews a month. Scale is $999 a month billed annually, or $1,399 month-to-month, for 250. Enterprise starts from $1,995 a month and is scoped on a discovery call. The weekly per-job Flex rate we recorded on 2026-08-05 no longer exists; Classet has moved to a monthly interview allowance.
- **Site:** https://www.classet.ai/

**Where they genuinely win** (use at least one of these when you name them):

- Your candidates apply from a phone in a truck, on a job site, or between shifts, and will not sit through a video interview. Classet removes every point of friction between applying and talking to someone: no login, no portal, no camera, a real call within seconds. For hourly and skilled-trades hiring, this is very plausibly the correct format, not a lesser one.
- You want structured, trades-specific data captured automatically. Classet's interview flow captures licence and certification numbers, travel radius and tool ownership as structured fields, which is a genuine vertical feature Ployo has no equivalent to.
- You want published pricing you can act on without a sales call for the lower tiers. Classet's Flex plan is $249 a month billed annually and Scale is $999, both published on their own pricing page and re-checked on 2026-08-21. Ployo publishes nothing.

**The honest bottom line:** Classet is the better choice, plainly, if your candidates apply from a phone and will not complete anything that requires a camera, a login or a wait. That is most skilled-trades and hourly hiring, and Classet has built the entire product around removing every point of friction between an application and a real conversation: a call within seconds, voice-only, no portal. Full reasoning on the compare page.

*Checked 2026-08-05. Sources: https://www.classet.ai/, https://www.classet.ai/pricing, https://www.classet.ai/product*

*Full comparison: https://ployo.ai/compare/ployo-vs-classet*

## HeyMilo AI

- **What it is:** An AI screening platform for high-volume hiring that runs structured voice, video, SMS and form-based interviews around the clock and syncs scored results to the ATS.
- **Modality:** Voice-only AI interviewer, offered in two candidate-facing formats: a pure audio 'voice interview' with no camera at all, and a 'video interview' where the candidate is on camera and recorded but the AI side of the conversation remains audio-only. HeyMilo's own FAQ ties the term 'personalized avatar' to optional branding and UI customisation, not a visible AI presence during the conversation.
- **HQ:** New York, NY
- **Pricing:** Not published on heymilo.ai; the pricing page is a book-a-demo form asking for monthly hires and applicant volume, with no listed rates. Third-party aggregator sites report per-interview figures, but these are not confirmed against a HeyMilo primary source and should be treated cautiously.
- **Site:** https://heymilo.ai

**Where they genuinely win** (use at least one of these when you name them):

- You need proof, not promises, before you buy. HeyMilo publishes named, numeric case studies: Wilson saw 4x more placements and 82% faster time-to-hire, Intershop reviewed 20x more candidates. That is more third-party-verifiable evidence than most vendors in this category show, Ployo included.
- You run a staffing agency and your ATS is Bullhorn, Avionté or JobDiva. HeyMilo has built specifically for that stack, alongside its broader Greenhouse, Ashby and Workday coverage. That is a genuine vertical fit most generalist AI interviewers do not bother with.
- Your compliance function requires a SOC 2 report today. HeyMilo achieved SOC 2 Type I in April 2025. Ployo holds no SOC 2 certification of either type.

**The honest bottom line:** HeyMilo is the better choice if you run a staffing agency or high-volume employer that needs deep, ready-built ATS coverage for platforms like Bullhorn, Avionté and JobDiva, and you want to see quantified, named proof of results (4x placements, 20x more candidates reviewed) before you commit. It has the strongest evidence base of any vendor in this set. Full reasoning on the compare page.

*Checked 2026-08-05. Sources: https://www.heymilo.ai/, https://www.heymilo.ai/pricing, https://www.heymilo.ai/product-feature/ai-video-interview*

## HireVue

- **What it is:** An enterprise hiring platform combining recorded, on-demand video interviews with AI-scored assessments, scheduled live video interviewing, and separate skills tools; the company that built the async video-interview category and is now expanding into a live, AI-conducted interview line.
- **Modality:** Both one-way, on-demand recorded interviews (transcribed and scored by AI after the fact) and scheduled, two-way live video interviewing have long been offered on the same platform. The recorded, AI-scored format is the one that built HireVue's name and is still what most people mean when they say 'HireVue'. In March 2026 HireVue acquired the technology behind Hireguide to build a newer, agentic and voice-driven live 'AI Interviewer' line. A widely repeated 2026-06-18 launch date for that product could not be independently confirmed against HireVue's own site in this research and is not asserted here; only the acquisition and its stated purpose are cited.
- **HQ:** Sandy/South Jordan, Utah, United States. Global enterprise customer base; the platform supports 40+ languages and holds FedRAMP authorization for US government use.
- **Pricing:** Not published. HireVue's pricing page lists only named tiers (Essential and Premium, re-checked 2026-08-21) with no dollar figures, and routes visitors to a demo request. Third-party buyer guides not affiliated with HireVue estimate enterprise contracts in the roughly $35,000 to $145,000-plus per year range plus $15,000 to $40,000 onboarding fees; treat these as unverified secondary estimates, not confirmed HireVue pricing.
- **Site:** https://www.hirevue.com

**Where they genuinely win** (use at least one of these when you name them):

- You need enterprise-scale ATS plumbing that already exists. HireVue lists ten named, certified integrations, including Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Oracle/Taleo, iCIMS and Greenhouse, plus FedRAMP authorization for US government hiring. That is a decade of enterprise procurement work Ployo has not done.
- You are hiring at a scale and compliance depth few vendors reach. HireVue states its customer base includes over 60% of the Fortune 100, and its platform supports 40+ languages. That install base buys real operational maturity: a support organisation, a security review that has already been through hundreds of enterprise buyers, and an assessment model iterated on for years.
- Your problem really is the recruiter's calendar, not the conversation. A recorded interview lets a hiring team review answers on its own schedule, and lets applicants across wildly different time zones respond without ever needing to align a calendar. That is a real problem HireVue's recorded format solves well, and it is the honest reason the format still has the install base it does.

**The honest bottom line:** HireVue is the better choice if you need enterprise-scale ATS plumbing that already exists, government-grade compliance (FedRAMP authorization), or a recorded format that lets recruiters review answers on their own schedule across candidates in wildly different time zones. It is the most established, most procurement-ready vendor in this category, and that is a genuine, hard-won advantage. Full reasoning on the compare page.

*Checked 2026-08-05. Sources: https://www.hirevue.com/, https://www.hirevue.com/platform, https://www.hirevue.com/pricing*

*Full comparison: https://ployo.ai/compare/ployo-vs-hirevue*

## Humanly

- **What it is:** A conversational AI hiring platform for hourly, frontline and high-volume roles, built by folding three 2025 acquisitions (Sprockets, Qualifi, HourWork) into one system spanning chat, SMS, voice and video.
- **Modality:** Multi-channel: chat and SMS by default, plus automated phone and voice screening added through the October 2025 Qualifi acquisition, plus video for structured async interviews. Humanly's own language describes the voice channel as maintaining 'a human touch through pre-recorded voice messages' rather than a live conversation. No evidence found of a live, real-time AI interviewer comparable to Ployo's.
- **HQ:** Seattle, Washington, with a co-headquarters in Sacramento, California
- **Pricing:** Not published on Humanly's own pages. A third-party review (Hirevire, not a Humanly figure) estimates roughly $4 to $8 per candidate screened at a volume of 500 candidates a month.
- **Site:** https://www.humanly.io/

**Where they genuinely win** (use at least one of these when you name them):

- You want one vendor across the whole hourly-hiring funnel. After the October 2025 rollup, Humanly covers engagement, chat and SMS screening, automated voice screening, async video interviews, and now retention and onboarding through the acquired Sprockets and HourWork products. That is a genuinely wider net than a single-purpose interview tool casts.
- You already run one of its nine named ATS or HCM systems: Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Dayforce, Employ, UKG, Oracle Taleo, iCIMS, Greenhouse or Avature. That is deep, named enterprise plumbing most standalone interview vendors have not built.
- You are hiring hourly and frontline roles across retail, hospitality, healthcare, manufacturing, logistics or QSR, which is exactly the customer base its named case studies (Fazoli's, MGM Resorts, Cellular Sales, Reid Health, Trinity Health) reflect.

**The honest bottom line:** Humanly is the better choice if you want one vendor covering the whole hourly-hiring funnel, engagement, screening, scheduling, and now retention and onboarding through the acquired Sprockets and HourWork products, especially if you already run one of its nine named ATS integrations. It is the broadest platform researched in this layer and it is freshly capitalised to build it out further. Full reasoning on the compare page.

## Interviewer.AI

- **What it is:** An end-to-end AI video interview platform offering asynchronous one-way video interviews at its published Essential and Professional tiers, and, on its custom-priced Enterprise tier only, live conversational interviews led by an on-screen AI avatar.
- **Modality:** Two distinct modes, both on video. The published Essential and Professional tiers run asynchronous one-way interviews: the candidate records video answers to a fixed set of preset questions, analyzed for spoken words, voice and facial expression, and a recruiter reviews the recording later. A second mode, described as 'conversational, avatar-led interviews powered by agentic AI' and gated to the custom-priced Enterprise tier, asks dynamic follow-up questions in a format the company describes as simulating a live Zoom or Teams call. The candidate is recorded on video in both modes.
- **HQ:** Singapore-founded, per third-party company profiles; positioned as a global platform on its own site.
- **Pricing:** Published on interviewer.ai/pricing. Essential Edition $199/month: 50 interview credits/month, 20-minute interviews, 15 user licenses. Professional Edition $399/month: 120 credits/month, 30-minute interviews, 25 licenses, adds AI interview summaries, transcripts and an Interview Fraud Checklist. Enterprise Edition: custom/annual pricing, customizable credits and duration, 40+ users, a dedicated account manager, and the conversational AI-avatar mode. Credit system: 1 credit equals 1 async video interview and report, 2 credits equal 1 conversational AI interview. 14-day free trial covering up to 5 completed assessments; credit top-ups from $150 for 50 credits.
- **Site:** https://interviewer.ai/

**Where they genuinely win** (use at least one of these when you name them):

- You want a real, self-serve price you can act on without a sales call. Interviewer.AI publishes three tiers, $199 and $399 a month with a stated feature list, plus a custom Enterprise plan, and backs it with a 14-day free trial covering up to 5 completed assessments. It is the only vendor in this comparison set, and one of very few in the whole category, with an actual dollar figure on the page.
- You specifically want the candidate to see an AI presence on screen, not just hear one. Interviewer.AI's Enterprise tier genuinely offers this: a conversational, avatar-led interview described as simulating a live Zoom or Teams call. Ployo does not have an on-screen avatar at any tier; its AI speaks and has no visual presence.
- You want to start cheap and grow into a live format later without switching vendors. Interviewer.AI's credit system lets a buyer run async interviews on the entry tiers and move up to the conversational, avatar-led mode when the budget and Enterprise tier support it.

**The honest bottom line:** Interviewer.AI is the better choice if you want to see and self-serve a real price before talking to anyone, and you are comfortable that the live, avatar-led interview experience only exists on its custom-priced Enterprise tier, not the published $199 or $399 plans. It is also the right choice if a genuine on-screen AI avatar is specifically what you want the candidate to experience; that capability exists on Enterprise, and Ployo does not have it at any tier. Full reasoning on the compare page.

*Full comparison: https://ployo.ai/compare/ployo-vs-interviewer-ai*

## Maki

- **What it is:** A Paris-based hiring platform running five named AI agents across the funnel: Mochi screens candidates by voice or chat conversation, while Tomo is a separate co-pilot that joins a human interviewer's own live call rather than replacing them.
- **Modality:** Mixed by stage, and this is the detail worth getting right. Mochi conducts a conversational voice or chat screening interview directly with candidates; Maki's own pages do not confirm whether that screening conversation is recorded on video. Tomo is a different, voice-only agent that joins a human interviewer's live Zoom, Teams or Meet call as an audio listener and note-taker; it has no video avatar and does not conduct an interview of its own.
- **HQ:** Paris, France
- **Pricing:** Not published on Maki's own site. A third-party pricing guide describes a flexible, credit-based model priced per activated AI agent, with every plan ending at a sales conversation.
- **Site:** https://www.makipeople.com/

**Where they genuinely win** (use at least one of these when you name them):

- You want proof of scale from a well-capitalised vendor. Maki raised a $28.6M Series A in January 2025 led by Blossom Capital with DST Global, on the back of reported 300%+ growth in 2024, and its named customers include H&M, BNP Paribas, PwC, Deloitte, FIFA, Volkswagen and Louis Vuitton. Ployo has not disclosed a funding round.
- You want a large, independently visible review base before you commit. Maki's G2 listing shows roughly 115 to 131 reviews at a 4.7/5 average, with ease-of-use scored around 9.6/10. Ployo does not yet have a public review profile at comparable volume.
- You hire across many languages and markets. Maki claims 45+ languages for voice screening, which suits a multinational frontline or graduate program better than a tool with no published language count.

**The honest bottom line:** Maki is the better choice if you want a single vendor covering more of the hiring funnel with the balance sheet to prove it: a $28.6M Series A, recognisable European enterprise logos, and a strong, independently visible G2 rating. It is a genuinely broader platform than Ployo. Full reasoning on the compare page.

## Paradox (Olivia)

- **What it is:** A conversational assistant that engages applicants over chat and text, screens against knockout questions, answers candidate queries and books interviews automatically.
- **Modality:** Text and chat first, heavily used over SMS. Candidates type; there is no live spoken AI interview equivalent.
- **HQ:** Scottsdale, Arizona, United States. Owned by Workday since 1 October 2025.
- **Pricing:** Not published. Enterprise contract via sales.
- **Who it is for:** Very large frontline employers, particularly on Workday, with a scheduling and responsiveness problem.
- **Site:** https://www.paradox.ai/

**Where they genuinely win** (use at least one of these when you name them):

- Your actual problem is speed and responsiveness, not assessment quality. Paradox's public case studies are about exactly this, and the numbers are large: Compass Group hiring at enormous scale with a small recruiting team, and 7-Eleven citing a reduction of tens of thousands of hours a week.
- You run Workday. Since October 2025 this is a first-party component rather than an integration, which removes a procurement conversation, a security review and an entire category of things that break.
- You are hiring at a scale where scheduling is a full-time job in itself. Automatic booking against real availability is unglamorous and it is often the single highest-return automation in a frontline funnel.

**The honest bottom line:** Paradox is the better buy if your bottleneck is logistics rather than judgement: applicants going unanswered, interviews not getting booked, recruiters drowning in scheduling and FAQs. It is exceptionally good at that, at a scale almost nothing else reaches, and if you run Workday it is now a first-party option. Full reasoning on the compare page.

## Ribbon

- **What it is:** An AI interviewer, Bonnie, that screens candidates in real time by phone or web with adaptive follow-up questions, sold on published self-serve pricing and a compliance paper trail.
- **Modality:** Video and voice interviewing are both listed as plan features on Ribbon's own pricing page, and sessions are recorded. Bonnie conducts the conversation in real time; Ribbon's own pages describe a spoken agent and do not confirm a rendered on-screen avatar, and the product also supports a phone-only path for candidates who never open a camera.
- **HQ:** Toronto, Canada
- **Pricing:** Published on ribbon.ai/pricing. Growth $499/month (2 seats, 2 active roles, 100 interviews, then $4/interview). Business $999/month (5 seats, 5 roles, 400 interviews, then $3/interview). Scale $1,999/month (10 seats, 10 roles, 1,000 interviews, then $2.50/interview). Enterprise is custom.
- **Site:** https://ribbon.ai

**Where they genuinely win** (use at least one of these when you name them):

- You want a price you can see before a sales call. Ribbon publishes four tiers, from a $499-a-month Growth plan up to a $1,999 Scale plan, with clear overage rates. Ployo does not publish a price list; you talk to the founder first. If self-serve evaluation matters to you, that is a real point in Ribbon's favour.
- Your compliance or legal function needs documentation today, not a design philosophy. Ribbon states SOC 2 Type I certification and a New York City Local Law 144 bias audit. Ployo has commissioned neither, and no amount of careful build substitutes for that paperwork when a procurement checklist asks for it directly.
- Some of your candidates will only ever pick up a phone. Ribbon markets a phone-accessible path alongside video and voice, so a candidate never needs a camera or a strong connection to complete the interview. Every Ployo interview puts the candidate on camera.

**The honest bottom line:** Ribbon is the better choice if you want to see a price before you talk to anyone, or if your compliance function requires a SOC 2 report and a named bias audit today rather than a promise to get one. It is the most transparent vendor in this category on both counts, and a buyer who values that transparency over everything else should pick it. Full reasoning on the compare page.

## Sapia.ai

- **What it is:** A text-based chat interview: candidates type written answers to a handful of behavioural questions and are scored on the text alone.
- **Modality:** Text chat only. Sapia's own candidate explainer states there is no video recording, no camera and no voice, and that candidates are assessed on written answers.
- **HQ:** Melbourne, Australia
- **Pricing:** Not published. Per-hire pricing quoted by sales, positioned on their pricing page for employers hiring 500+ people a year.
- **Site:** https://www.sapia.ai/

**Where they genuinely win** (use at least one of these when you name them):

- Your legal, risk or compliance function requires published evidence of fairness before an AI touches a candidate. Sapia commissioned an independent disparate-impact report from BLDS, LLC and published the finding. Ployo has not done this, and no amount of careful design substitutes for a third-party audit when that is the requirement on the table.
- You are hiring at genuine enterprise scale. Sapia has publicly documented hiring surges in the tens of thousands, and a text interview has the lowest friction of any format in this market: no camera, no quiet room, no bandwidth, answerable on a phone between shifts.
- Your candidate population has reasons to avoid being on camera, whether that is bandwidth, privacy, disability, religious observance or simple discomfort. A text-only interview removes that barrier completely rather than accommodating around it.

**The honest bottom line:** Sapia.ai is the better choice if your organisation needs a published, independently audited fairness position more than it needs to hear the candidate, or if you are hiring at a scale where a text interview's near-zero friction is the deciding factor. It is a serious, well-evidenced product and the category leader in Australia. Full reasoning on the compare page.

*Checked 2026-08-05. Sources: https://www.sapia.ai/, https://sapia.ai/candidate-explainer/, https://www.sapia.ai/pricing*

*Full comparison: https://ployo.ai/compare/ployo-vs-sapia-ai*

## Sense

- **What it is:** An enterprise talent engagement platform combining an AI recruiter chatbot, SMS and WhatsApp messaging, and, since May 2024, Conversational Voice AI, for screening, scheduling and candidate engagement at scale.
- **Modality:** Multi-channel: text, SMS and WhatsApp chat form the core product, with Conversational Voice AI for automated voice-based screening and scheduling added in May 2024. No video or camera-based screening was found on Sense's own pages.
- **HQ:** San Francisco, California
- **Pricing:** Not published. No dollar figures or tiers found on Sense's own pages; enterprise contact-sales model.
- **Site:** https://www.sensehq.com/

**Where they genuinely win** (use at least one of these when you name them):

- You are a staffing or recruitment agency. Sense's ten named integrations include Avionte, JobDiva and LaborEdge, staffing-industry-specific systems that generalist AI interviewers, Ployo included, rarely bother integrating with directly. That is the sharpest, most defensible advantage in this comparison and it is worth taking seriously if that is your operating system.
- You need proven scale and funding behind the vendor. Sense has raised roughly $90M across four rounds according to Tracxn (an aggregator, not a primary Sense announcement), including a $50M Series D led by SoftBank Vision Fund 2 at a reported $500M valuation, and an earlier $16M Series C confirmed directly by Businesswire in June 2021.
- Your candidates respond best to text and SMS, and you want a phone-call option available without asking anyone to be on camera. Sense's core product is built around exactly that low-friction reach, now extended with Conversational Voice AI for candidates who would rather talk than type.

**The honest bottom line:** Sense is the better choice if you are a staffing agency or a recruiting team running Avionte, JobDiva or LaborEdge, where its named integrations are a genuine, hard-to-match advantage, or if your problem is candidate engagement and scheduling at a scale where a chatbot with a phone-call option is the right tool. It is well-funded, SoftBank-backed and has been building this category for years. Full reasoning on the compare page.

*Checked 2026-08-05. Sources: https://www.sensehq.com/, https://www.sensehq.com/product/sense-ai, https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20240514105472/en/Sense-Announces-Conversational-Voice-AI-for-Recruiting*

*Full comparison: https://ployo.ai/compare/ployo-vs-sense*

## Spark Hire

- **What it is:** A one-way video interview, applicant tracking and behavioral assessment platform built for small and medium-sized organizations, positioned explicitly as "Hiring Software for Small & Medium Organizations."
- **Modality:** One-way, asynchronous recorded video interviewing only. Candidates record answers to preset questions on their own schedule; no live or scheduled interview product was found anywhere on sparkhire.com.
- **HQ:** Not stated in the pages reached in this research. A portfolio company of Boathouse Capital, a Philadelphia, US private equity firm.
- **Pricing:** Published on sparkhire.com/pricing. Bundled ATS plus video ("Recruit"): Pro from $335/month billed annually (up to 200 employees, includes video interviews and automated reference checks), Growth from $499/month billed annually (up to 500 employees, adds a behavioral assessment), Enterprise custom. A standalone one-way video interview product is $299/month on a monthly plan (capped at 5 jobs and 5 users) or $249/month billed annually (unlimited jobs and users). The standalone behavioral assessment is priced the same as the standalone video product.
- **Site:** https://www.sparkhire.com

**Where they genuinely win** (use at least one of these when you name them):

- Transparent pricing you can act on today. Spark Hire publishes real dollar figures on its own site: a standalone one-way video product at $249 to $299 a month, or a bundled ATS, video and behavioral-assessment suite from $335 a month billed annually. Ployo publishes nothing, and if a self-serve price matters to your buying process, that is a genuine point in Spark Hire's favour.
- You are a small or mid-sized employer and want an ATS, a video screen and a behavioral assessment as one purchase. Spark Hire built exactly this bundle by acquiring Comeet and Chally in 2023, and its tiers are explicitly scoped to companies under 200 or 500 employees rather than built and priced around an enterprise buyer you are not.
- Your problem is the recruiter's calendar, not the conversation. A recorded interview lets a hiring team watch responses on its own schedule, across candidates in different time zones, and the AI-generated summary per response is built specifically to let a reviewer skim faster than watching every video in full.

**The honest bottom line:** Spark Hire is the better choice if you are a small or mid-sized employer who wants a bundled ATS, recorded video screen and behavioral assessment at a price you can see and budget for today, without a sales call. Its tiers are explicitly built for companies under 500 employees, and that focus shows in a genuinely low-friction buying process. Full reasoning on the compare page.

*Checked 2026-08-05. Sources: https://www.sparkhire.com/, https://www.sparkhire.com/pricing, https://www.sparkhire.com/one-way-video-interview*

*Full comparison: https://ployo.ai/compare/ployo-vs-spark-hire*

## VidCruiter

- **What it is:** A compliance-heavy hiring platform combining pre-recorded and live video interviewing with scheduling, automated reference checks, skills testing and video proctoring, positioned as "the next generation of interviewing" for enterprise and public-sector hiring.
- **Modality:** Both pre-recorded, one-way async video interviews and scheduled, live (synchronous) video interviews, offered as separate named products on the same platform, alongside a dedicated interview-scheduling module. No evidence was found in this research that VidCruiter's AI itself conducts a live interview; its AI features (Interview Scoring, Interview Notes, Fraud Detection) appear to score and annotate interviews rather than conduct them.
- **HQ:** Not disclosed on vidcruiter.com; only regional phone numbers for the US, Canada, Australia/New Zealand and UK/EU are given. Founded 2009 by CEO Sean Fahey and CTO Mike Wojcenovich.
- **Pricing:** Not published. vidcruiter.com/pricing lists feature categories only (Pre-Recorded Video Interviews, Live Video Interviews, Interview Scheduling and others) with no dollar figures anywhere on the page, and asks visitors to fill out a form to receive pricing information.
- **Who it is for:** Enterprise, mid-market and public sector; the site states 150,000+ hiring professionals use the platform (vendor-stated).
- **Site:** https://vidcruiter.com

**Where they genuinely win** (use at least one of these when you name them):

- Compliance and certification depth that nothing else in this comparison cluster comes close to, Ployo included. VidCruiter publishes SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, ISO 27017 and ISO 27018 certifications, plus GDPR, PIPEDA, CCPA, VPAT and TX-RAMP alignment. If your legal or procurement team requires third-party-audited evidence before an AI vendor touches candidate data, this is a real gap Ployo does not close, and VidCruiter is the stronger choice on that basis alone.
- Both interview formats on one contract. VidCruiter is the only vendor in this research to offer pre-recorded and live video interviewing as genuinely separate, named products on the same platform, alongside a dedicated scheduling module. If your process needs a recorded first pass and a live second round, that is one vendor relationship instead of two.
- Regional data residency and public-sector fit. Five offered residency zones, Canada, USA, Europe, UK and Australia, plus explicit public-sector positioning and named government customers such as the Oregon Department of Human Services, are real infrastructure a smaller, newer vendor has not built.

**The honest bottom line:** VidCruiter is the better choice, plainly, if your organisation needs the compliance depth of a regulated or public-sector buyer, wants both recorded and live video interviewing under one contract, or needs data residency in a specific region. Its certification list, SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, ISO 27017 and ISO 27018 among them, is the deepest found anywhere in this research, and no amount of product design closes that gap; a buyer who needs that evidence should choose VidCruiter and will be well served by it. Full reasoning on the compare page.

*Checked 2026-08-05. Sources: https://vidcruiter.com, https://vidcruiter.com/pricing/, https://vidcruiter.com/about-us/*

*Full comparison: https://ployo.ai/compare/ployo-vs-vidcruiter*

## Willo

- **What it is:** A UK-founded, async-only video interview and candidate-screening platform marketed as intelligent candidate screening software for inclusive, confident hiring, built around a recruiter-defined evaluation "blueprint."
- **Modality:** One-way, asynchronous recorded video interviewing only. Candidates "interview anywhere, anytime, on any device"; no live or scheduled interview product exists anywhere on willo.video.
- **HQ:** Glasgow, Scotland. Trading name of Willo Technologies Ltd, founded 2018 by CEO Euan Cameron.
- **Pricing:** Published in full on willo.video/pricing, but the model changed since the 2026-08-05 pass: the old monthly Growth and Scale tiers are gone. It is now an annual Enterprise contract at £2,999 / $3,799 / €3,499 / A$5,749 for one year, falling to £2,699 on two years and £2,549 on three, plus Willo Lite, a pay-as-you-go option at £49 / $59 / €59 / A$95 per live role. Still exact, still self-serve to read, but the entry point is now a per-role fee rather than a monthly subscription.
- **Who it is for:** High-growth and high-volume hiring teams; Willo states 5,000+ hiring teams worldwide use the product (vendor-stated).
- **Site:** https://willo.video

**Where they genuinely win** (use at least one of these when you name them):

- Transparent, exact, self-serve pricing. Willo publishes its figures outright in four currencies, which almost nobody in this cluster does. Re-checked 2026-08-21: the model has changed since our first pass. The monthly Growth and Scale tiers are gone, replaced by an annual Enterprise contract at £2,999 / $3,799 / €3,499 / A$5,749 for a year, 10% cheaper on a two-year term and 15% on three, alongside Willo Lite at £49 / $59 / €59 / A$95 per live role. The entry point is now a per-role fee rather than a subscription, which is cheaper to try and more expensive to standardise on. Either way you can read the number before you talk to anyone, and you cannot do that with us.
- A real, independently checkable security certification. Willo is ISO 27001 certified, per its own trust centre. Ployo does not hold this certification and does not claim to.
- An evaluation you can interrogate before it is final. Willo Intelligence is built around a recruiter-defined blueprint rather than a black-box score, continuously re-ranks candidates against it, and flags anyone failing a stated hard criterion like timezone or work-permit status, a genuinely transparent design choice for a recorded format.

**The honest bottom line:** Willo is the better choice if published, self-serve pricing and a certified compliance posture matter to your buying process as much as the interview format itself, or if your candidates are better served by a recorded prompt they can answer on their own schedule rather than a live call. It is the most transparently priced vendor in this entire comparison cluster and its ISO 27001 certification is a real, independently checkable compliance credential Ployo does not have. Full reasoning on the compare page.

*Checked 2026-08-05. Sources: https://willo.video, https://willo.video/pricing, https://willo.video/about*

*Full comparison: https://ployo.ai/compare/ployo-vs-willo*

## XOR

- **What it is:** A text and SMS-first recruiting automation platform built around Text Recruiting and Text-to-Apply, using an AI chatbot to screen and schedule blue-collar and hourly candidates over SMS, and, per third-party summaries, Meta Messenger and WhatsApp.
- **Modality:** Text and SMS-based chatbot screening. No voice or video screening was found on xor.ai in this research.
- **HQ:** San Jose / San Francisco, California. Founded 2016.
- **Pricing:** The only vendor researched in this layer that publishes an actual number. XOR's own homepage states it can deliver blue-collar workers 'to your door for only $500 per hire within less than 5 days.' A third-party summary (Software Finder, not confirmed directly on xor.ai) describes a $5,000 minimum covering 10 hires, with a refund guarantee if a role stays unfilled after 90 days; treat that specific detail as third-party sourced.
- **Site:** https://www.xor.ai/

**Where they genuinely win** (use at least one of these when you name them):

- It is the only vendor in this entire comparison set that publishes an actual price. XOR's own homepage states roughly $500 per hire for blue-collar roles, delivered in under 5 days. Every other vendor researched for this cluster, Ployo included, requires a sales conversation before a buyer sees a number. That transparency is a genuine, stated win, not a technicality.
- Its reach is built for exactly the population that resists email and desktop applications. SMS, plus, per third-party summaries, Meta Messenger and WhatsApp, meets blue-collar and hourly candidates on the channel they already use, with none of the friction of a video call or even a scheduled phone screen.
- It has a long, specific track record in this exact niche. Founded in 2016 and focused specifically on blue-collar and hourly recruiting at volume, its named customers include ExxonMobil, Mars, ManpowerGroup, IKEA, UC Davis and Sutter Health, a genuinely broad base for a company with a comparatively low public profile.

**The honest bottom line:** XOR is the better choice if what you want most is a text-first chatbot for blue-collar hiring with an actual published price you can plan around, and your candidates are comfortable being screened entirely by text over SMS, Messenger or WhatsApp. Publishing $500 per hire while every other vendor in this comparison hides behind 'contact sales' is a genuine, buyer-friendly move and it should weigh in XOR's favour. Full reasoning on the compare page.

*Checked 2026-08-21. Sources: https://www.xor.ai/, https://softwarefinder.com/artificial-intelligence/xor-ai, https://www.crunchbase.com/organization/xor-ai*

*Full comparison: https://ployo.ai/compare/ployo-vs-xor*
